title: Former Mexican soccer goalkeeper charged in $5.4 million counterfeit watch scheme tied to Laredo
excerpt: A former professional goalkeeper who played for Atlas, Santos Laguna and Necaxa is charged with trafficking in counterfeit goods after federal authorities say his Laredo import-export business moved fake luxury watches worth about $5.4 million.
content:
A former Mexican professional soccer goalkeeper has been charged with trafficking in counterfeit goods in a federal case tied to a Laredo import-export business, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.

Pedro Hernandez-Calderon, 45, a Mexican citizen, is a former professional goalkeeper who played for Mexican clubs Atlas, Santos Laguna and Necaxa, federal prosecutors said. He remains in custody pending further criminal proceedings.

According to the criminal complaint, authorities seized four counterfeit luxury watches on Oct. 5 in Anchorage, Alaska, that were destined for a Laredo warehouse. Authorities in Alaska coordinated with law enforcement in South Texas to identify those responsible, prosecutors said.

The charges allege Hernandez-Calderon operated an import-export business that received counterfeit watches in Laredo for shipment to customers in Mexico. Between June 2025 and October 2026, authorities identified numerous shipments of counterfeit watches to Laredo addresses with an estimated retail value of approximately $5.4 million if the watches had been genuine, according to the complaint. Prosecutors said investigators also uncovered photographs, communications and shipping records documenting the operation, and representatives of luxury watch manufacturers confirmed the watches submitted for review were counterfeit.

If convicted, Hernandez-Calderon faces up to 10 years in federal prison and a possible $2 million fine. The investigation was conducted by Homeland Security Investigations with the assistance of IRS Criminal Investigations and the U.S. Postal Service, and Assistant U.S. Attorney Thomas Sekula is prosecuting the case, according to the Justice Department.

A criminal complaint is a formal accusation of criminal conduct, not evidence, and a defendant is presumed innocent unless convicted through due process of law.

Update — November 12, 2026

Hernandez-Calderon was arrested in Laredo on November 4, and appeared before U.S. Magistrate Judge Diana Song Quiroga on November 5, who ordered him held in custody while the case proceeds, according to Vocifera and El Heraldo de Veracruz. His defense is scheduled to argue for his release on bond at a hearing on Thursday, November 12, contending he is not a flight risk despite his ties in Mexico. The outcome of that hearing had not been reported as of this update. The charges remain allegations, and Hernandez-Calderon is presumed innocent unless convicted through due process of law.

Sources: U.S. Department of Justice, Southern District of Texas; Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 11, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 10, 2026; Vocifera, Nov. 10, 2026; El Heraldo de Veracruz, Nov. 11, 2026.
